newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Petrochem union to go on partial strike.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Petrochem union to go on partial strike.

text.p: The unionised workers of Hyundai Petrochemical Co, a unit of South Korea's giant Hyundai Group, will go on partial strike on Wednesday in protest at the new labour law, a union official said on Tuesday.
"Hyundai Petrochemical unionists will have a partial strike from 4:30 p.m. (0730 GMT)," the official said.
This will affect some 900 union workers, he added. Hyundai Petrochemical has a total workforce of 1,500.

The official said Hyundai Petrochemical's factories would continue to run, but the strike was expected to have an impact on production. He was unable to give an estimate of expected loss in production.
The union, an affiliate of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, would expand the action to an all-out strike if the confederation called for one, the official said.
"In that case, all production could be halted," he said.
Unions at 13 of the Hyundai Group's affiliates have already walked out since Monday.
The 13 affiliates include Hyundai Precision and Industry Co Ltd, Hyundai Motor Service Co Ltd, and Hyundai Mipo Dock Yard Co Ltd.

Strikes have crippled much of South Korean industry since a new labour law allowing lay-offs, flexible work hours and the replacement of striking workers was railroaded through parliament on December 26.
